questions.question: A 30-second audio clip becomes an input representation before a decoder emits tokens. What broad model shape is described?
options: A nearest-neighbor classifier
A transformer encoder-decoder
A single recurrent predictor
A convolutional generator only
questions.explanation: Whisper encodes log-mel audio, then an autoregressive transformer decoder generates text while cross-attending to encoder states. The “single recurrent predictor” option misses this encoder-decoder split and the decoder’s attention over encoded audio.

questions.question: Whisper uses a fixed 30-second input window. How does the lesson handle clips of different lengths?
options: Zero-pad clips shorter than 30 s and chunk longer clips
Drop all content after the first 30 s for every clip
Combine all clips into one 30 s spectrogram
Stretch every clip to 30 s by changing the sample rate
questions.explanation: The model has a 30-second window: shorter clips are padded to it, while longer recordings are split into windows. Truncation loses later speech; chunking lets the system process the full long recording.

questions.question: Which decoder prompt task token requests English translation from non-English speech?
options: The no-timestamps token
The translate task token
The transcribe task token
The end-of-text token
questions.explanation: The translate task token requests English output from non-English audio; the language tag identifies the language and transcribe asks for verbatim text. Transcribe preserves the spoken language rather than requesting translation into English.

questions.question: What architectural change makes Large-v3-turbo faster than Large-v3 in this lesson?
options: It uses a 4-layer decoder instead of 32 layers
It replaces all token outputs with frame labels
It doubles the decoder depth and narrows attention
It removes the audio encoder and log-mel input
questions.explanation: Turbo reduces decoder depth from 32 layers to four, cutting autoregressive work while retaining the encoder and log-mel input. The lesson attributes the speed change to a shallower decoder; the audio encoder remains part of the model.

questions.question: A two-second speech clip is padded to Whisper’s fixed input window and produces text during trailing silence. Which handling reduces unsupported transcript text?
options: Keep required padding, then check transcript segments against detected speech.
Remove all fixed-window padding and decode the short mel tensor directly.
Increase decoder temperature until silent frames produce different text.
Carry previous text into the padding so every silent frame has a prompt.
questions.explanation: Whisper still pads short speech-containing clips to its fixed decoding window. Compare transcript segment timestamps with detected speech regions, using confidence or no-speech evidence as appropriate, to reject text unsupported by speech. Removing mandatory padding breaks the input contract; carrying previous text into silence can encourage continuation.

questions.question: A 10-minute recording uses 30-second chunks with 5 seconds of overlap. How many chunks does the lesson’s schedule produce?
options: 24 chunks
120 chunks
30 chunks
20 chunks
questions.explanation: The schedule advances by 30 − 5 = 25 seconds; starts at 0, 25, …, 575 give 24 chunks for 600 seconds. Twenty is 600/30 with no overlap; the five-second overlap shortens the step and adds four starts.
